The authorized release may begin only when the planned scope has been approved, the required test set for that exact scope has passed, a named fallback operator has accepted the shift, and the operations owner has given the final go-ahead. Retain material population, timeframe and attribution when reporting measurements. A forwarded copy is not a second observation. [B1: Approved baseline]
Programme owner Mira Vale signed the baseline on 12 November 2026 at 10:00 UTC. It planned a 20 November rollout to 120 field coordinators across six depots, using the desktop planner and the mobile rescheduling flow. The baseline included the four readiness conditions in ALDER-RULES R3; the date was a plan, not permission to launch regardless of readiness.

[B2: Responsibilities]
Theo Lane is responsible for QA evidence. Sol Reed is responsible for operating readiness and the final go-ahead. Mira owns programme scope and schedule decisions. Operations must nominate a fallback operator and record that person's acceptance before go-ahead. The baseline does not name that operator.

[B3: Working estimate]
The product team estimated that the full six-depot rollout might eventually save 40 coordinator hours per week. This was a planning estimate, not a measured benefit, and it applied to the full desktop-plus-mobile scope.

documents.text:
[Q1: Test evidence]
At 14:00 UTC, QA lead Theo Lane recorded 18 of 18 required desktop-planner checks passed for the two-depot, 30-coordinator configuration. The linked matrix was still awaiting attachment at 16:00 UTC. Eight volunteer desktop users logged a median task time of six minutes during a two-day rehearsal, compared with a self-reported earlier median of nine minutes. There was no randomized comparison, and a trainer was present during rehearsal. These observations do not establish that the software alone caused the reduction or that all 30 rollout users will see the same change.
